question: What does the idiom "Barking up the wrong tree" mean?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Blaming the wrong person**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Barking up the wrong tree"** means to direct your efforts or complaints at the wrong person or thing. (गलत व्यक्ति को दोष देना)
 
 
• **Example:** If you think I’m responsible for the mistake, you’re barking up the wrong tree.
 
 
• **Blaming the wrong person** refers to accusing or holding someone responsible for something they are not actually responsible for. (गलत व्यक्ति को दोष देना)
 
 
• **Example:** The manager was barking up the wrong tree by blaming the intern for the error when it was a system glitch.
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "Barking up the wrong tree" aligns with the meaning of **Blaming the wrong person**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Blaming the wrong person**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: Finding the right solution** (सही समाधान ढूँढना): Refers to identifying the correct way to address a problem or resolve an issue.
 
 
• **Example:** After hours of brainstorming, the team finally found the right solution to the technical issue.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Avoiding confrontation** (टकराव से बचना): Refers to steering away from arguments, conflicts, or disputes.
 
 
• **Example:** He avoids confrontation by keeping his opinions to himself during heated discussions.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Taking unnecessary risks** (अनावश्यक जोखिम लेना): Refers to engaging in actions that involve danger or high stakes without a valid reason.
 
 
• **Example:** Jumping off cliffs without safety equipment is an example of taking unnecessary risks.
